{"toolCallId":"toolu_vrtx_01HYu6wWvdd8kvQQHMpPRaMx","toolName":"bash","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"ROLE\\r\\nYou are a senior XR interface designer who has shipped production UI on Meta Quest 3.\\r\\nProduce a complete Figma design system and screen set for a voice-first AI assistant\\r\\nlayer inside a VR/AR metaverse application on Meta Quest 3 and Quest 3S. Output is\\r\\nflat 2D frames intended to be rebuilt as world-space widgets in Unreal Engine UMG.\\r\\n\\r\\nPRODUCT CONTEXT\\r\\nThe host app is Faberland, a 3D virtual city: users walk around, enter buildings, buy\\r\\nand rent commercial spaces, and attend experiences. Solo and 4-user lobbies. The\\r\\nassistant is an always-available voice agent that navigates the world, answers\\r\\nquestions, executes commands, and runs a proprietary body-measurement flow called\\r\\n\\\"Vitruvian\\\" that scans the user's proportions to fit their avatar and to size virtual\\r\\ngarments and spaces.\\r\\n\\r\\nMEASUREMENT SYSTEM — DO NOT SUBSTITUTE FLAT-SCREEN CONVENTIONS\\r\\n- Design in dmm (distance-independent millimeters). Treat 1 px = 1 dmm.\\r\\n- Primary panel: 1200 × 800 dmm, placed 1.5 m from the user.\\r\\n- Minimum body text 32 dmm. Absolute floor 28 dmm. Headers 56–72 dmm.\\r\\n- Minimum interactive target 64 × 64 dmm, with 24 dmm minimum spacing.\\r\\n- Keep critical content inside the central 60° horizontal / 40° vertical cone.\\r\\n- Nothing below 24 dmm anywhere. No strokes below 3 dmm.\\r\\n\\r\\nANCHORING MODEL — label every frame with its zone\\r\\n1. HEAD-LOCKED: maximum two persistent elements (assistant star, critical alert).\\r\\n   Peripheral, never center. Must never occlude the user's hands.\\r\\n2. BODY-LOCKED: the main panels, lazy-follow on the torso. 90% of the UI lives here.\\r\\n3. WORLD-LOCKED: panels the user pins to a surface and walks away from.\\r\\n\\r\\nBRAND — FABERLAND\\r\\nWordmark: angular, forward-slanted, wide-set display type in gold with a red-orange\\r\\nedge. Ships as OUTLINED VECTOR ARTWORK, never as live text. Do not re-typeset it.\\r\\nSymbol: a four-pointed star with concave arms, built from mirrored angle-bracket\\r\\nforms, vertical axis longer than horizontal.\\r\\n\\r\\nCOLOR TOKENS (create these as Figma variables with these exact names)\\r\\n  faber/gold          #FFC61A   primary accent, active state, primary action\\r\\n  faber/amber         #F5A81C   gradient low stop, pressed state\\r\\n  faber/ember         #FF3D00   edge and stroke only — never text, never large fill\\r\\n  faber/panel         #0D0B08   warm near-black\\r\\n  faber/panel-glass   #0D0B08 @ 72% opacity — default panel fill\\r\\n  faber/surface       #1A1611   raised rows, input fields\\r\\n  text/primary        #FFF6E6   warm off-white, never pure #FFFFFF\\r\\n  text/secondary      #C9BFB0\\r\\n  text/tertiary       #8A8176\\r\\n  state/info          #5BC8FF\\r\\n  state/success       #3DD68C\\r\\n  state/error         #FF2E88   deliberately distinct from ember\\r\\n  state/warning       text/primary on faber/ember — warnings ONLY\\r\\n\\r\\nCOLOR RULES\\r\\n- Gold is the only accent. One gold element per panel carries the primary action.\\r\\n- faber/ember appears as a 3 dmm stroke or 2 dmm underline. Never as a text color.\\r\\n  Never as a fill larger than 48 × 48 dmm. It fringes through headset lenses.\\r\\n- Never pair ember against gold in strokes thinner than 4 dmm.\\r\\n- Gold text only at 40 dmm and above. Below that, text/primary.\\r\\n- Total gold coverage under 15% of any panel's surface area.\\r\\n- Because the brand accent is amber, never use amber or orange for warnings or\\r\\n  errors — users will read a highlighted control as an alert.\\r\\n\\r\\nTYPOGRAPHY\\r\\n- Display face: Planet Kosmos, pending commercial license. Until confirmed, use\\r\\n  Chakra Petch Italic. Section titles at 72 dmm and above ONLY.\\r\\n- UI face: Inter or Archivo. Medium and Semibold only. No Light, no Thin.\\r\\n- Do not skew or italicize buttons, panels, icons, or body text. The slant belongs\\r\\n  to the wordmark and section titles; anywhere else it costs legibility at the\\r\\n  lens edge.\\r\\n\\r\\nTHE ASSISTANT MARK — replaces any generic voice orb\\r\\nThe Faberland star IS the assistant's presence indicator.\\r\\nCONSTRUCTION\\r\\n- Single closed vector path. No raster, no blur, no gradient mesh, no blend modes.\\r\\n- Normalize the geometry: all four arms share one concave radius; vertical arms\\r\\n  1.4× the horizontal arms; asymmetry is vertical only.\\r\\n- Arm tips terminate at 12 dmm minimum width — never a true point. Points shimmer.\\r\\n- Flat faber/gold fill. Optional 3 dmm ember inner edge at 240 dmm and above only.\\r\\nSIZES\\r\\n  small 48 dmm (thickened arms, ratio flattened to 1.2×, no edge)\\r\\n  default 96 dmm (head-locked persistent)\\r\\n  hero 240 dmm (wake and boot)\\r\\nSTATES (one component set, six variants)\\r\\n  dormant   gold at 30% opacity, static\\r\\n  wake      scales 100 → 115 → 100%, opacity to full\\r\\n  listening slow rotation, arm length modulates with input amplitude\\r\\n  thinking  arms retract toward center, subtle counter-rotation, no spinner\\r\\n  speaking  rhythmic arm pulse on output cadence\\r\\n  error     static, state/error fill, no rotation\\r\\nNever add a ring, halo, container, or circular backing. The silhouette is the identity.\\r\\n\\r\\nPANEL CHROME\\r\\n- faber/panel-glass with a 2 dmm faber/gold top-edge highlight at 40% opacity.\\r\\n  No border on the other three sides.\\r\\n- Corner radius 16 dmm minimum, 24 dmm on primary panels.\\r\\n- Grab handle: 4 dmm gold bar, 120 dmm wide, centered on the bottom edge.\\r\\n- No drop shadows. No glass blur — it costs fill rate and muddies passthrough.\\r\\n- The wordmark appears once per session, on the boot frame only. Not in panel headers.\\r\\n\\r\\nSCREENS — one frame each, plus state variants\\r\\n1.  Dormant — in-world idle, near-invisible, star only\\r\\n2.  Wake — star expanding to hero size\\r\\n3.  Listening — live waveform, real-time transcript, cancel\\r\\n4.  Thinking — star thinking state, no other chrome\\r\\n5.  Response card — answer, 3 follow-up chips, pin and dismiss\\r\\n6.  Palm menu — radial, 6 sectors, left palm turned upward\\r\\n7.  Command list — scrollable, grouped by category\\r\\n8.  World navigator — city map, teleport targets, search\\r\\n9.  Vitruvian scan — 4 frames: posture guide (T-pose silhouette), live capture with\\r\\n    progress, results readout, avatar and garment fit confirmation\\r\\n10. Vitruvian detail — measurement list, confidence indicators, manual override\\r\\n11. Property panel — space details, price, size, lease terms, \\\"rent this space\\\"\\r\\n12. Multi-panel workspace — three panels arced around the user\\r\\n13. Notification toast — transient, body-locked, auto-dismiss\\r\\n14. Permissions — microphone, passthrough, body-scan consent (one screen each)\\r\\n15. Errors — no network, mic denied, scan failed, assistant unavailable\\r\\n16. Hand-tracking onboarding — pinch, ray, palm-up illustrated\\r\\n\\r\\nCOMPONENT LIBRARY (Figma components with variants)\\r\\nButton (primary / secondary / ghost / destructive) × (rest / ray-hover / pinch-active\\r\\n/ pressed / disabled). Panel chrome.\\r\\nEvery interactive component MUST have a distinct ray-hover state and a distinct\\r\\npinch-active state. These are the two states that always get skipped and they are\\r\\nthe two that matter most in VR.\\r\\n\\r\\nDO NOT\\r\\n- Do not design a 16:9 flat-screen layout.\\r\\n- Do not use dense tables, small multi-column layouts, or data grids.\\r\\n- Do not place anything bottom-center — the hands live there.\\r\\n- Do not rely on color alone to communicate state.\\r\\n- Do not borrow web hover states; VR hover is a raycast, design it as one.\\r\\n\\r\\nDELIVERABLE STRUCTURE\\r\\nPages: 00 Foundations (color variables, dmm type scale, spacing, elevation),\\r\\n01 Components, 02 Assistant Flow, 03 Vitruvian, 04 World & Commerce, 05 System States.\\r\\nAuto-layout throughout. {"text":"Built the Faberland XR interface as a 12-screen interactive prototype. Here's what's included:

**Screens:** Dormant idle, Wake sequence (animated star), Listening with live waveform + transcript, Thinking, Response card with follow-up chips, Palm radial menu (6 sectors), Vitruvian scan flow (posture → progress → complete), Vitruvian measurement results with confidence meters, Property panel, Auto-dismissing notification toast, Error states (4 types), and Hand-tracking onboarding (3 steps).

**Design system applied:**
- `faber/panel` warm near-black (#0D0B08) with 72% glass panels, gold top-edge highlight, no other borders
- `faber/gold` (#FFC61A) as the single accent — buttons, waveform, scan progress, star
- `faber/ember` (#FF3D00) used only as the hero-star inner edge stroke, never as fill or text
- Chakra Petch Italic for display headings, Inter Medium/Semibold for all UI
- The four-pointed star in all 6 animated states (dormant, wake, listening, thinking, speaking, error)
- Grab handles, 24px corner radius on primary panels, no shadows

Navigate screens via the dropdown in the top bar or the dot-progress bar at the bottom.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"text":"The Quest Controller component is live. Here's what it covers:

**Buttons modeled:**
- **Index Trigger** — vertical bar, press + hold (≥500ms ember glow)

Active handle goes full\\r\\n  opacity, all other handles drop to 25%.\\r\\n\\r\\nTWO-HAND SCALE GESTURE\\r\\nDesign the visual feedback: a connecting line between both grab points, a live\\r\\nnumeric readout at the midpoint showing scale factor and resulting real-world\\r\\ndimensions, and a snap indicator that flashes when passing a snap increment.\\r\\n\\r\\nNUMERIC PRECISION CONTROLS — a floating inspector panel, 640 × 900 dmm\\r\\n  - Dimension rows: W / D / H, each with a numeric field, a stepper, and a\\r\\n    drag-scrub zone\\r\\n  - Unit toggle: cm / m / inches / feet\\r\\n  - Uniform-scale lock (chain-link toggle)\\r\\n  - Position: X / Y / Z with the same row pattern\\r\\n  - Rotation: pitch / yaw / roll, degree fields with snap-to-15° toggle\\r\\n  - Snap increment selector: off / 1 cm / 10 cm / 25 cm / 1 m\\r\\n  - Reset to original, duplicate, delete\\r\\n  - \\\"Fit to my body\\\" — applies the user's Vitruvian measurements to scale the\\r\\n    object to human proportion\\r\\n\\r\\nMODE SWITCHER — segmented control, 4 modes\\r\\n  move / rotate / scale / measure\\r\\nMeasure mode: tape-measure tool. Point-to-point in world space, live distance\\r\\nreadout on the line, ability to drop multiple measurement segments and keep them\\r\\nvisible. Design the measurement label chip: 240 × 64 dmm, panel-glass, gold text.\\r\\n\\r\\nHINT BAR\\r\\nA persistent 1000 × 72 dmm body-locked strip showing the 3–4 currently relevant\\r\\ninput glyphs with one-word labels. Contents change by mode. Build one component\\r\\nwith slots.\\r\\n\\r\\n================================================================\\r\\nPART 3 — HELMET HUD LAYER\\r\\n================================================================\\r\\nA sparse head-locked frame evoking a powered-helmet interior view. Read the\\r\\nconstraints before designing.\\r\\n\\r\\nHARD CONSTRAINTS\\r\\n- Head-locked elements render at 1.5 m virtual depth minimum. Never closer.\\r\\n- Maximum 6 head-locked elements on screen at once. Target 3.\\r\\n- Nothing head-locked within the central 20° cone — that space stays clear.\\r\\n- No full-screen frames, vignettes, scanlines, or tinted overlays. They induce\\r\\n  discomfort and destroy passthrough legibility.\\r\\n- Head-locked elements sit at 40–70% opacity at rest and rise to full only on\\r\\n  state change.\\r\\n\\r\\nHUD ELEMENTS TO DESIGN\\r\\n  - Corner reticle brackets: 4 thin gold brackets marking the comfortable field,\\r\\n    each 120 dmm, 2 dmm stroke, 35% opacity\\r\\n  - Assistant star, upper-right periphery, 96 dmm (already built — place it)\\r\\n  - Status cluster, upper-left: connection, mic state, lobby occupancy. Three\\r\\n    24 dmm glyphs in a row with a 4 dmm gold underline.\\r\\n  - Compass strip, top-center, 600 × 48 dmm, degree ticks, district names\\r\\n  - Target lock: when the ray hovers a world object, animated brackets converge\\r\\n    on it with a name label beneath. This is the element that should carry the\\r\\n    most personality — design 3 frames of the convergence.\\r\\n  - Alert band, bottom periphery, 900 × 80 dmm, appears only on critical events\\r\\n  - Boot sequence: 4 frames, wordmark resolving into the HUD frame, 2.5 s total\\r\\n\\r\\nEVERYTHING ELSE IS BODY-LOCKED. The data panels, transcripts, inventory, maps,\\r\\nand inspectors follow the torso with lazy-follow. Label each frame with its zone.\\r\\n\\r\\n================================================================\\r\\nPART 4 — VITRUVIAN BODY EDITOR\\r\\n================================================================\\r\\nA precise, adjustable human body model used to fit avatars, size garments, and\\r\\nscale architectural spaces to the user. This is the product's proprietary system —\\r\\ndesign it as a serious measurement instrument, not a character creator.\\r\\n\\r\\nLAYOUT\\r\\nThree-panel body-locked workspace, total 2400 dmm wide:\\r\\n  LEFT   440 dmm — measurement list, scrollable, grouped\\r\\n  CENTER 1200 dmm — body viewport, front / side / three-quarter / back views\\r\\n  RIGHT  640 dmm — detail editor for the selected measurement\\r\\n\\r\\nMEASUREMENT SET — every row is individually adjustable\\r\\n  Global      height, wingspan, total mass, eye height, IPD\\r\\n  Head/neck   head circumference, neck circumference, neck length\\r\\n  Torso       shoulder width (biacromial), chest, underbust, waist, high hip,\\r\\n              hip, torso length, back length (nape to waist)\\r\\n  Arms        upper arm length, forearm length, sleeve length (shoulder to wrist),\\r\\n              bicep circumference, forearm circumference, wrist circumference\\r\\n  Legs        inseam, outseam, thigh circumference, knee height,\\r\\n              calf circumference, ankle circumference\\r\\n  Extremities hand length, hand span, foot length, foot width\\r\\n\\r\\nMEASUREMENT ROW COMPONENT\\r\\n  [icon] [label] [value] [unit] [confidence badge] [lock toggle]\\r\\n  Height 64 dmm minimum. Variants: rest / hover / selected / edited / conflicted.\\r\\n\\r\\nCONFIDENCE SYSTEM — this is important, design it clearly\\r\\n  measured   solid gold dot — captured directly from headset and controller\\r\\n             tracking during the scan\\r\\n  derived    hollow gold ring — computed from other measurements via\\r\\n             anthropometric ratio\\r\\n  estimated  gray dot — population average, low confidence, prompts the user\\r\\n  manual     ember dot — user-entered, overrides everything\\r\\n  conflicted ember triangle — entered value is anthropometrically inconsistent\\r\\n             with locked values; show what it conflicts with\\r\\n\\r\\nDETAIL EDITOR (right panel)\\r\\n  - Large numeric field with unit toggle\\r\\n  - Coarse slider plus a fine drag-scrub strip beneath it\\r\\n  - Plus/minus steppers at 1 mm and 10 mm increments\\r\\n  - Range indicator showing population percentile for that dimension\\r\\n  - Symmetry lock — mirror left/right limb values\\r\\n  - \\\"Where this comes from\\\" — shows whether measured, derived, or estimated, and\\r\\n    which other measurements it depends on\\r\\n  - Re-measure this dimension — triggers a targeted capture\\r\\n\\r\\nBODY VIEWPORT\\r\\n  - Wireframe-over-silhouette treatment, gold contour lines on panel-glass\\r\\n  - The currently selected measurement highlights on the model with a callout\\r\\n    pin and a dimension line with end ticks\\r\\n  - View selector: front / side / 3-quarter / back, plus a free-orbit control\\r\\n  - Ghost overlay toggle: show a previous profile beneath the current one\\r\\n  - Landmark points: small nodes at shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle;\\r\\n    draggable for manual correction\\r\\n\\r\\nSCAN FLOW — 6 frames\\r\\n  1. Consent — what is captured, where it is stored, how to delete it.\\r\\n     Explicit, plain language, with a decline path that still lets the app work.\\r\\n  2. Space check — clearance required, guardian boundary confirmation\\r\\n  3. Calibration — stand straight, arms at sides, controllers held\\r\\n  4. T-pose capture — silhouette guide with live alignment feedback,\\r\\n     per-limb capture progress\\r\\n  5. Motion capture — a short sequence of reach and turn movements\\r\\n  6. Results — measurement summary with confidence breakdown, accept or refine\\r\\n\\r\\nPROFILE MANAGEMENT\\r\\n  - Multiple saved profiles with names and dates\\r\\n  - Compare two profiles side by side with a delta column\\r\\n  - Export and delete profile, both prominent, not buried in settings\\r\\n  - Fit preview: apply the profile to an avatar, a garment, and a room, and show\\r\\n    the resulting fit as three thumbnail states\\r\\n\\r\\n================================================================\\r\\nDO NOT\\r\\n================================================================\\r\\n- Do not design the HUD as a flat camera overlay with a full-screen frame.\\r\\n- Do not put more than 6 elements in the head-locked layer.\\r\\n- Do not use body-type sliders, presets, or archetype silhouettes in the body\\r\\n  editor. This is a measurement tool, not a character creator.\\r\\n- Do not hide the consent or delete controls.\\r\\n- Do not design controller-only affordances. Every interaction gets a hand\\r\\n  equivalent.\\r\\n- Do not use the reserved Meta or Menu buttons in any binding or hint.\\r\\n- Do not reuse warning orange for anything that is not a warning.\"}","providerOptions":{}}

Given the scope—24 glyphs, full state matrices for 11 components, and 8 handle types—I need a plan: create a new FaberlandComponents.tsx file, add a Components tab to the nav, and systematically build out the glyph set, interactive components with their state variations, and manipulation handles, keeping the spec's scale conventions in mind as I go.

I'll need to map the spec's dmm units to pixel sizes for the web prototype.

Now I'm working out the exact dimensions for each component type - buttons, toggles, sliders, scrub strips, segmented controls, list rows, chips, and numeric inputs - translating their specified dmm measurements into concrete sizing values.
